main.title: Tekken 7
main.subtitle: Follow the arcade debut and the later home versions of Tekken 7
main.summary: Tekken 7 is a 2015 fighting game developed by Bandai Namco Studios and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment.

cards.heading: The 2015 arcade debut and later home editions
cards.text: Tekken 7 is a 2015 fighting game developed by Bandai Namco Studios and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment. It is the seventh main and ninth overall installment in the Tekken series, and is the first in that series to be released for PC. Tekken 7 was released to arcades in March 2015. An updated arcade version, Tekken 7: Fated Retribution, was released in July 2016, and features expanded content including new stages, costumes, items and characters. The home versions released for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One in June 2017 were based on Fated Retribution.

cards.heading: The Mishima conflict, new mechanics and reception
cards.text: Set shortly after the events of Tekken 6, the plot focuses on the events leading up to the final battle between martial artist Heihachi Mishima and his son, Kazuya. Tekken 7 introduces several new elements to the fighting system, such as Rage Arts and the Power Crush mechanic, making the game more beginner friendly than previous iterations in the series. Tekken 7 was a critical and commercial success, selling 12 million copies as of July 2024. A sequel, Tekken 8, was released on January 26, 2024.

main.title: Bloodborne
main.subtitle: Yharnam Rewards the Player Who Advances into Fear
main.summary: Bloodborne encourages the wounded hunter to make a difficult choice: withdraw, or strike quickly enough to recover.

cards.heading: Enter Yharnam as a hunter
cards.text: Bloodborne arrived on PlayStation 4 in 2015 with Yharnam's streets and inhabitants as its threatening introduction. FromSoftware's hunter must study opponents while exploring the city. The original launch guidance treats caution as useful preparation, but it also gives players a strong reason to move towards danger after being hit.

cards.heading: An injury opens a short opportunity
cards.text: Lost health briefly remains recoverable through successful attacks. That window makes an injury into a decision: try to win the health back now, or retreat and spend a healing item. An aggressive response can help, but repeating it without reading the enemy can turn one mistake into another.

cards.heading: Learn what the weapon can become
cards.text: Trick weapons change form, altering their attacks and reach. Firearms and carefully timed responses add further possibilities, while Blood Vials supply healing. Learning a fight consequently involves more than memorising a safe distance. The hunter's available tools can change that distance and the opportunities worth pursuing.

cards.heading: Cooperative play and Chalice Dungeons
cards.text: The game includes online multiplayer features. Players can summon others for cooperative play, invade other players' worlds for player-versus-player combat, and leave messages that appear in other players' games. Bloodborne also features Chalice Dungeons, optional dungeons accessed through ritual items. Some Chalice Dungeons have fixed layouts, while "root" versions use procedural generation to create new arrangements of rooms, enemies, and rewards.

main.title: Pillars of Eternity
main.subtitle: The Classic CRPG Returns Because Its Audience Was Waiting
main.summary: Pillars of Eternity used crowdfunding to support a new role-playing world built around the strengths of older computer RPGs.

cards.heading: Ask the audience to back a new world
cards.text: Obsidian announced in March 2015 that Pillars of Eternity had gone gold, with release set for 26 March on Windows, Mac and Linux. The project began its crowdfunding campaign in September 2012 as Project Eternity. Kickstarter and PayPal contributions together brought in more than four million dollars.

cards.heading: Recognisable influences, original rules
cards.text: The studio named Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale and Planescape: Torment among its influences. It was making a new setting and rules rather than another licensed entry in those series. That combination offered backers something recognisable while giving the team room to build a world whose details it controlled.

cards.heading: From a campaign to a finished game
cards.text: The finished release followed roughly two and a half years of development. The funding story makes the relationship between audience and production unusually visible: players committed support before there was a completed game to buy. Obsidian's gold announcement marks the point where that proposal became software ready for release.

cards.heading: Creating a character and choosing skills
cards.text: Character creation affects more than combat. Race, background, attributes and class can open choices in conversations and encounters. Eleven classes bring different tools: a cipher attacks through souls, while a druid can transform into a beast. Skills such as Mechanics or Lore also change what the party can open, understand or use. Experience comes from quests and other situations rather than simply killing enemies, so avoiding a fight need not mean losing progress. The proprietary rules resemble the party-based role-playing tradition while giving different character builds practical ways through the same problem.
